As the parameter $α$ increases, the contribution from the fast Dirac cone becomes dominant. The additional transitions involving the flat bands and the fast Dirac cone substantially reduce the region where undamped plasmons can exist, similarly to the conventional $α-\mathcal{T}_3$. Consequently, stable plasmons are observed only for relatively small values of $α$ or at very small wave vectors. These unusual electronic and collective properties make the Kek-$α$ model a promising platform for future plasmonic and nanoscale electronic applications.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a theoretical and numerical investigation of polarization, plasmons, and plasmon damping in the Kek-α model, a hybrid 2D material combining α-T₃ lattice and Kekulé-distorted graphene features. The model has two degenerate flat bands and two Dirac cones with different Fermi velocities (fast and slow). Undamped plasmons exist only for small α or small wave vectors due to additional particle-hole transitions, making the model promising for plasmonic applications.
AI.motivation: To understand the unusual electronic and collective properties of the Kek-α model—a new 2D material that combines features of the α-T₃ lattice and Kekulé-distorted graphene—and to characterize its plasmon excitations and damping mechanisms, which differ fundamentally from conventional Kek-Y graphene.
AI.method: Rigorous theoretical and numerical investigation of the polarization function, plasmon dispersion, and Landau damping in the Kek-α model, including analysis of the low-energy band structure (two degenerate flat bands and two inequivalent Dirac cones) and the particle-hole continuum structure.
AI.result: The particle-hole continuum has two distinct branches from transitions between the Dirac cones, plus an additional particle-hole mode above the main diagonal from electron transitions involving the fast Dirac cone. As α increases, fast-cone contributions dominate. These extra transitions shrink the undamped plasmon region, so stable plasmons exist only for small α or very small wave vectors.
AI.conclusion: The Kek-α model exhibits unusual electronic and collective properties—flat bands, two Dirac cones with different Fermi velocities, and constrained undamped plasmon regions—making it a promising platform for future plasmonic and nanoscale electronic applications.

title: Enhanced and robust superconductivity in La0.8Sr0.2NiO2 membranes compressed up to 210 GPa
summary: The discovery of superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelate thin films has opened a new frontier for exploring unconventional oxide superconductors beyond the copper oxide family. However, the presence of substrate hampers investigations under very high pressure. Recently, this problem was circumvented by a study of freestanding Nd0.85Sr0.15NiO2 membranes, which revealed that superconducting transition temperature kept increasing as the pressure was ramped up to 91 GPa, without showing signs of saturation. Naturally, one wonders what would happen at even higher pressures. Here, we report that superconductivity in a freestanding La0.8Sr0.2NiO2 membrane persists under applied ultrahigh pressures up to 210 GPa. The superconducting transition onset temperature exhibits a continuous dome-like evolution, increasing from 16 K at ambient pressure to a peak of 74.5 K at 146 GPa, and then gradually decreasing to 57.4 K at 210 GPa. Such robustness of superconductivity against ultrahigh pressure has not been observed in high-Tc oxide superconductors before.

AI.tldr: This paper reports that superconductivity in a freestanding La0.8Sr0.2NiO2 membrane persists up to ultrahigh pressures of 210 GPa, with a dome-like evolution of Tc that peaks at 74.5 K under 146 GPa before decreasing to 57.4 K at 210 GPa—a robustness not previously observed in high-Tc oxide superconductors.
AI.motivation: Infinite-layer nickelate thin films offer a new frontier for unconventional superconductivity beyond cuprates, but the substrate limits high-pressure studies. Previous work on freestanding Nd0.85Sr0.15NiO2 showed Tc kept increasing up to 91 GPa without saturation, raising the question of what happens at even higher pressures.
AI.method: The study uses freestanding La0.8Sr0.2NiO2 membranes to remove substrate effects, allowing electrical transport measurements under applied ultrahigh pressures up to 210 GPa.
AI.result: Superconductivity persists up to 210 GPa. The transition onset temperature follows a continuous dome-shaped evolution: 16 K at ambient pressure, rising to a maximum of 74.5 K at 146 GPa, then declining to 57.4 K at 210 GPa.
AI.conclusion: The robustness of superconductivity under ultrahigh pressure up to 210 GPa is unprecedented among high-Tc oxide superconductors, demonstrating that nickelate superconductors can sustain superconductivity across an exceptionally wide pressure range.

title: Inhomogeneous Ising Model on 2D kagomé Lattice: Fermionic field approach
summary: We investigate the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Ising model (2DIM) on the kagom'e lattice by mapping it onto a particular non-symmetric eight-vertex model and constructing the corresponding $R$-matrix. Using a fermionic representation, we evaluate the partition function and derive explicit expressions for the main thermodynamic quantities. In the thermodynamic limit, we obtain an exact equation for the critical surface determining the phase transition of the model. We also calculate the free energy, specific heat, and spontaneous magnetization in the ferromagnetic case. Furthermore, we show that when one or two coupling constants vanish, the model reduces, respectively, to the square-lattice and one-dimensional Ising models. In both limits, our results reproduce the corresponding exact critical couplings and free energies.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Ising model on the kagome lattice by mapping it to a non-symmetric eight-vertex model, constructing the R-matrix, and using fermionic representation to derive exact thermodynamic quantities including an exact critical surface equation, free energy, specific heat, and spontaneous magnetization.
AI.motivation: To extend exact solvability of Ising-type models to the inhomogeneous case on the kagome lattice, which has not been fully treated, and to unify results with the square-lattice and 1D Ising models as limiting cases.
AI.method: The model is mapped to a non-symmetric eight-vertex model and an R-matrix is constructed. A fermionic representation is then used to evaluate the partition function and derive thermodynamic quantities in the thermodynamic limit.
AI.result: An exact equation for the critical surface is obtained. Explicit expressions for the free energy, specific heat, and spontaneous magnetization in the ferromagnetic case are derived, and the model correctly reduces to the square-lattice and 1D Ising models when one or two couplings vanish, reproducing exact critical couplings and free energies.
AI.conclusion: The inhomogeneous Ising model on the kagome lattice is exactly solvable via the eight-vertex mapping and fermionic approach, and encompasses the square-lattice and 1D Ising models as special limits.

title: Configuration averaging of X-ray absorption spectra of disordered systems within the augmented-space full multiple-scattering formalism
summary: We present a formulation of the full multiple-scattering theory of X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) for disordered systems based on the augmented-space method of Mookerjee. Both substitutional (chemical) and thermal (vibrational) disorder are cast, on the same footing, as exact matrix elements of a non-random operator acting on an enlarged Hilbert space. The configuration-averaged scattering-path operator is thereby obtained by inverting a non-random secular matrix, with no expansion in scattering paths, without recourse to the single-site approximation and without any assumption on the shape of the disorder distribution. This is what the quantitative analysis of the near-edge region requires: XANES lies where the multiple-scattering series does not converge, so that a treatment of disorder tied to a path expansion is unavailable there. The inversion is carried out by a continued-fraction (Lanczos) recursion, which accesses the required matrix element without constructing the full configuration basis or diagonalising the augmented operator. The operator Debye-Waller factor of the harmonic theory is recovered as the Gaussian special case, and anharmonic disorder is included with no additional machinery, through the moments of a non-Gaussian displacement distribution. Where the series does converge, the construction also settles a question of principle: for statistically independent site variables, replacing each t-matrix by its configuration average is exact only for scattering paths in which every site occurs once, and for paths that revisit a site we obtain the exact second-order correction.

AI.tldr: A formulation of full multiple-scattering XAS theory for disordered systems using the augmented-space method, treating substitutional and thermal disorder as non-random matrix elements in an enlarged Hilbert space, enabling configurational averaging via continued-fraction inversion without path expansion or single-site approximation.
AI.motivation: Quantitative XANES analysis requires a disorder treatment that does not rely on the multiple-scattering series expansion, since XANES lies in the region where that series does not converge. Prior disorder treatments tied to path expansion are therefore unavailable at the near-edge.
AI.method: Both substitutional and thermal disorder are cast as exact matrix elements of a non-random operator in an enlarged Hilbert space via the augmented-space method of Mookerjee. The configuration-averaged scattering-path operator is obtained by inverting a non-random secular matrix using continued-fraction (Lanczos) recursion, avoiding full basis construction and diagonalization. No single-site approximation or assumption on disorder distribution shape is required.
AI.result: The operator Debye-Waller factor of harmonic theory is recovered as the Gaussian special case; anharmonic disorder is included through moments of non-Gaussian displacement distributions. For convergent series, replacing each t-matrix with its configuration average is shown to be exact only for scattering paths where every site occurs once, and exact second-order corrections are derived for paths that revisit sites.
AI.conclusion: The method provides a rigorous, distribution-agnostic framework for configuration-averaged XAS that works in the XANES region and also settles a question of principle about the validity of single-site t-matrix averaging in path-expansion regimes.

title: Diodes and capacitors for the transport of monopoles in fragmented spin ice
summary: Spin-ice materials are famous for their quasi-particle excitations that behave like magnetic monopoles. Magnetricity is the concept that these monopoles can conduct an AC magnetic current, in analogy with conduction electrons. While monopole dynamics has been intensively studied and is reasonably well understood, very little has been done to design devices in order to control magnetricity. Here we develop a theoretical proof of concept for the design of diodes and capacitors for the transport of monopoles. We use the property of systems with magnetic fragmentation, where spin-ice physics co-exists with long-range antiferromagnetic order. The key point is that magnetic order allows for the existence of domain walls. Under certain conditions of preparation, this domain wall is equivalent to an asymmetric filter for monopoles. In a given direction, positive charges can go through while negative ones are repelled; the opposite applies in the opposite direction. This asymmetry effectively functions like a diode for monopole current. Successive domain walls separate positive from negative charges with a vacuum of charge in between, producing a capacitor for monopoles. Once the capacitor is charged, it can in principle be used as a battery for monopoles. All microscopic mechanisms are explained and our proof of concept is validated by simulations of more than a million spins. Application to experiments are discussed for rare-earth pyrochlore oxides and artificial spin ice. Finally, we discuss in general terms how a domain wall in fragmented spin ice can also be seen as an emergent boundary separating two mirror "worlds" separated by time-reversal symmetry. Beyond spin ice, our work opens a promising direction of investigation for the dynamics of emergent quasi-particles crossing domain walls in chiral and nematic spin liquids, which also possess a broken symmetry.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a theoretical proof of concept for designing diodes and capacitors that control the flow of magnetic monopoles in fragmented spin-ice materials, where domain walls act as asymmetric filters for monopole transport. Validated by simulations of over a million spins, the work also discusses potential applications in pyrochlore oxides, artificial spin ice, and emergent boundary physics in other spin liquids.
AI.motivation: While monopole dynamics in spin-ice materials are well understood, almost no work has been done on designing functional devices to control magnetricity (AC magnetic current carried by monopoles). The authors aim to fill this gap by proposing concrete device concepts—diodes and capacitors—for monopole transport.
AI.method: The authors exploit magnetic fragmentation, where spin-ice physics coexists with long-range antiferromagnetic order. The key mechanism is that magnetic order permits domain walls, which under appropriate preparation conditions act as asymmetric filters for monopoles: in one direction positive charges pass while negatives are repelled, and vice versa in the opposite direction. They explain the microscopic mechanisms and validate the concept via large-scale simulations (over one million spins).
AI.result: The domain walls in fragmented spin ice effectively operate as diodes for monopole currents. Successive domain walls separate positive and negative charges with a charge vacuum in between, forming a capacitor (which can be charged and potentially used as a monopole battery). Simulations of over one million spins confirm the proposed mechanisms. Applications are discussed for rare-earth pyrochlore oxides and artificial spin ice, and the domain wall is interpreted as an emergent time-reversal boundary between two mirror worlds.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes a theoretical foundation for functional circuit-like devices for magnetic monopole transport. Beyond spin ice, it suggests a promising avenue for studying emergent quasi-particles crossing domain walls in other symmetry-broken systems such as chiral and nematic spin liquids.

title: Microwave Response of the Superconducting Diode Effect in Proximitized Bilayer Graphene Interferometers
summary: Microwave irradiation has emerged as a promising means to tune the superconducting diode effect (SDE) in Josephson junction devices. Previous experimental studies have mainly focused on the adiabatic-driving regime, in which the diode efficiency increases monotonically with microwave power and can approach the ideal value of unity. Beyond this regime, however, the microwave response of the SDE remains largely unexplored experimentally. In this work, we investigate the microwave response of the SDE in bilayer-graphene-based superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs) under a broad range of driving frequencies. We show that increasing the driving frequency changes the response characteristics of the diode efficiency to microwave power--the dependence of the diode efficiency evolves from monotonic enhancement with increasing microwave power in the adiabatic regime to non-monotonic behavior beyond this regime, and ultimately to sign-reversal as well oscillatory characteristics at sufficiently high frequencies. We find that these experimentally observed frequency-dependent power response characteristics of the diode efficiency can be qualitatively captured by simulations based on the resistively shunted junction model using the device current-phase relations extracted from the experiments. These results establish SQUIDs made from bilayer graphene as a versatile platform for studying dynamic properties of superconducting junction devices.

AI.tldr: This paper experimentally investigates the microwave response of the superconducting diode effect (SDE) in bilayer-graphene-based SQUIDs across a broad range of driving frequencies, revealing a transition from monotonic enhancement of diode efficiency in the adiabatic regime to non-monotonic, sign-reversing, and oscillatory behavior at higher frequencies. The observed responses are qualitatively captured by resistively shunted junction model simulations using experimentally extracted current-phase relations.
AI.motivation: Previous experimental studies of microwave-tuned SDE in Josephson junctions focused mainly on the adiabatic-driving regime where diode efficiency increases monotonically with microwave power. The microwave response of the SDE beyond this regime remains largely unexplored experimentally, motivating this investigation across a broad frequency range.
AI.method: The authors investigate the microwave response of SDE in bilayer-graphene-based superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs) under a broad range of driving frequencies. They compare experimental diode efficiency behaviors with simulations based on the resistively shunted junction (RSJ) model, using current-phase relations extracted from the experimental devices.
AI.result: Increasing the driving frequency changes the diode efficiency's power-response characteristics: from monotonic enhancement in the adiabatic regime, to non-monotonic behavior beyond this regime, and ultimately to sign-reversal and oscillatory characteristics at sufficiently high frequencies. These experimental observations are qualitatively captured by RSJ-based simulations.
AI.conclusion: Bilayer-graphene-based SQUIDs serve as a versatile platform for studying dynamic superconducting junction properties, and the work extends understanding of non-adiabatic microwave-driven SDE behavior beyond previously explored regimes.

title: Pressure-induced concurrent amorphization and superconductivity in topological material NbNiTe5
summary: We have systematically studied the structural and electronic properties of a topological material NbNiTe5 under high pressure. The evolution of the normal state resistance shows a non-monotonic trend from 0.7 GPa to 5.1 GPa, in accordance with the second-order transition along the inter-layer direction observed in X-ray diffraction and Raman spectra. At around 10 GPa, the sample starts amorphization, which is concurrent with the emergence of superconductivity. Upon further compression, the structural disorder enhances and the superconducting transition becomes clearer, suggesting that the superconductivity is modulated by the degree of disorder in NbNiTe5 under high pressure. Within 45.7 GPa, the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) slowly rises from 0.6 K at 9.5 GPa to 1.4 K at 45.7 GPa. Our findings extend the family of transition metal chalcogenide superconductors and shed new light on understanding superconductivity in disordered systems.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically investigates the structural and electronic properties of the topological material NbNiTe5 under high pressure, finding that superconductivity emerges concurrently with pressure-induced amorphization around 10 GPa, with Tc gradually rising from 0.6 K at 9.5 GPa to 1.4 K at 45.7 GPa, modulated by the degree of structural disorder.
AI.motivation: To extend the family of transition metal chalcogenide superconductors and gain new understanding of how superconductivity emerges and is modulated in disordered systems, using NbNiTe5 (a topological material) under high pressure as a platform.
AI.method: Systematic high-pressure experiments combining electrical resistance measurements (to track normal state resistance and superconducting transitions), X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy (to probe structural changes including a second-order transition along the inter-layer direction and amorphization).
AI.result: Resistance evolves non-monotonically from 0.7 to 5.1 GPa in agreement with a second-order inter-layer transition. Amorphization begins around 10 GPa, coinciding with the onset of superconductivity. Further compression enhances structural disorder and sharpens the superconducting transition. Tc rises slowly from 0.6 K at 9.5 GPa to 1.4 K at 45.7 GPa.
AI.conclusion: Superconductivity in NbNiTe5 under high pressure is directly modulated by the degree of structural disorder, and the findings expand the family of transition metal chalcogenide superconductors while offering new insights into superconductivity in disordered systems.

title: Front Selection Is Not Determined by Renormalization-Group Stability
summary: The Fisher--Kolmogorov--Petrovsky--Piskunov equation provides a paradigmatic example of front propagation and asymptotic-state selection. Using a unified renormalization-group (RG) framework, we show that its traveling-wave solutions form a continuous family of RG fixed points and that all fronts with $v \ge 2$ are RG-stable. Nevertheless, the asymptotically selected front is not determined by RG stability. The FKPP equation therefore provides an explicit example in which RG fixed-point stability and asymptotic-state selection are distinct concepts.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that the FKPP equation's traveling-wave solutions form a continuous family of renormalization-group (RG) fixed points, all stable for v ≥ 2, yet the asymptotically selected front is not determined by RG stability—providing an explicit example where RG fixed-point stability and asymptotic-state selection are distinct concepts.
AI.motivation: To clarify the relationship between RG fixed-point stability and asymptotic-state selection in the FKPP equation, a canonical model for front propagation and state selection.
AI.method: A unified renormalization-group (RG) framework is applied to analyze the traveling-wave solutions of the FKPP equation, examining the stability of the continuous family of RG fixed points.
AI.result: All traveling-wave fronts with velocity v ≥ 2 are RG-stable, forming a continuous family of RG fixed points; however, the asymptotically selected front is not determined by RG stability, demonstrating that these two concepts are independent.
AI.conclusion: The FKPP equation serves as an explicit counterexample showing that RG fixed-point stability and asymptotic-state selection are distinct concepts that must not be conflated.

title: Resonant Raman spectroscopies beyond density-functional theory
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Supplemental Material included (5 pages, 4 figures)
summary: Resonant Raman spectroscopy probes, in a single measurement, how electrons and phonons couple in a material. Density-functional theory (DFT) typically reproduces well phonon frequencies, but resonant Raman intensities hinge on electron-phonon matrix elements and electronic transitions that are far more sensitive to the underlying exchange-correlation approximation. However, electron-phonon coupling has so far been accessible only through linear-response theories developed for a handful of semilocal DFT methods, leaving the sensitivity of resonant Raman intensities to the electronic-structure approximation essentially unexplored. Here, we introduce a general finite-difference framework that can compute resonant Raman tensors for any electronic-structure method capable of delivering forces, eigenvalues, and wavefunctions of pristine and displaced configurations. We apply the formalism to graphene and monolayer MoS$_2$, using hybrid functionals or meta-GGAs, and show that these approaches systematically enhance electron-phonon couplings relative to semilocal DFT, reflecting reduced dielectric overscreening. A decomposition of the Raman tensor shows that accurate intensities require electronic eigenvalues and electron-phonon matrix elements to be treated consistently at the same level of theory. Among the approaches tested, hybrid functionals provide the best overall agreement with experiment. Because the framework needs only quantities every electronic-structure code already produces, it opens the door to systematic, beyond-DFT Raman characterization or benchmarking against experiments, especially for 2D materials.

AI.tldr: A general finite-difference framework computes resonant Raman tensors for any electronic-structure method that can provide forces, eigenvalues, and wavefunctions. Applied to graphene and monolayer MoS2, it shows hybrid functionals and meta-GGAs enhance electron-phonon couplings relative to semilocal DFT, with hybrid functionals giving the best experimental agreement.
AI.motivation: Resonant Raman intensities are highly sensitive to the exchange-correlation approximation via electron-phonon matrix elements and electronic transitions, yet electron-phonon coupling has only been accessible through linear-response theories limited to a few semilocal DFT methods, leaving the sensitivity of resonant Raman intensities to the electronic-structure approximation unexplored.
AI.method: A general finite-difference framework is introduced that computes resonant Raman tensors using only forces, eigenvalues, and wavefunctions of pristine and displaced configurations—quantities any electronic-structure code already produces. It is applied to graphene and monolayer MoS2 using hybrid functionals and meta-GGAs, with a decomposition of the Raman tensor to analyze the contributions.
AI.result: Hybrid functionals and meta-GGAs systematically enhance electron-phonon couplings relative to semilocal DFT, reflecting reduced dielectric overscreening. A decomposition shows accurate intensities require consistent treatment of electronic eigenvalues and electron-phonon matrix elements at the same level of theory. Hybrid functionals provide the best overall agreement with experiment.
AI.conclusion: The framework opens the door to systematic beyond-DFT Raman characterization or benchmarking against experiments, especially for 2D materials, since it only requires quantities every electronic-structure code already produces.

title: Microscopic magnetic phase evolution in the Weyl semimetal Mn$_3$Sn revealed by $μ^+$SR
comment: 13 pages total (8 pages main text, 5 pages appendix and references), 7 Figures
summary: We report a comprehensive muon spin relaxation ($μ^+$SR) and bulk magnetization study of the antiferromagnetic (AFM) Weyl semimetal Mn$_3$Sn (composition Mn$_{2.99}$Sn). Mn$_3$Sn is reported to exhibit a commensurate inverse triangular (IT) AFM phase, an incommensurate (IC) helical AFM phase, and a proposed low-temperature spin-glass-like state. In our sample, we establish the respective transition temperatures for these phases to be $T_\mathrm{N} = 418$ K, $T_\mathrm{t} \approx 275$ K, and $T_\mathrm{f} = 21$ K. Investigating the low-temperature regime below $T_\mathrm{f}$, we find no evidence of a static spin-glass state. Instead, the sample exhibits an increasing ferromagnetic (FM) component accompanied by a localized slowing of spin fluctuations, indicating that these phenomena may be decoupled. In the IC helical AFM phase, fitting the zero-field (ZF) spectra reveals an asymmetric internal magnetic-field distribution, indicating that the magnetic structure is heavily modified by anharmonicity. Upon warming above 150 K, a continuous redistribution of muon spectral weight reveals a broad regime of coexisting local magnetic environments associated with the IC helical and IT-AFM phases. In the commensurate IT-AFM phase above $T_\mathrm{t}$, a persistent missing fraction in the initial asymmetry indicates that a subset of implanted muons, corresponding to roughly 20% of the sample-related asymmetry, undergoes unresolved ultrafast depolarization. Finally, we observe temperature-driven shifts in muon site populations above 325 K. Ultimately, our results show a highly dynamic magnetic landscape in Mn$_3$Sn, demonstrating how its complex magnetic orders often coexist and evolve continuously with temperature.

AI.tldr: A comprehensive muon spin relaxation and magnetization study of the antiferromagnetic Weyl semimetal Mn2.99Sn reveals no static spin-glass state below Tf=21K (instead an increasing FM component with decoupled localized spin fluctuations), a heavily anharmonic-modified asymmetric field distribution in the IC helical phase, broad coexistence of IC helical and IT-AFM magnetic environments above 150K, a persistent missing fraction (~20%) in the IT-AFM phase indicating ultrafast muon depolarization, and temperature-driven muon site population shifts above 325K.
AI.motivation: To comprehensively characterize the magnetic phases and transitions in the antiferromagnetic Weyl semimetal Mn3Sn, particularly to resolve the nature of its proposed low-temperature spin-glass-like state and to understand how its multiple complex magnetic orders (commensurate inverse triangular AFM, incommensurate helical AFM) evolve and coexist across temperature.
AI.method: The study employs muon spin relaxation (μ+SR) and bulk magnetization measurements on Mn2.99Sn. Zero-field μ+SR spectra were fitted to extract internal magnetic-field distributions, initial asymmetry (tracking missing fractions), and muon site populations as a function of temperature across all three reported phases.
AI.result: Transition temperatures established at TN=418K, Tt≈275K, and Tf=21K. No static spin-glass state is found below Tf. The IC helical phase shows asymmetric internal field distribution from anharmonicity. Above 150K, coexisting IC helical and IT-AFM local magnetic environments appear. In the IT-AFM phase, ~20% missing sample asymmetry indicates ultrafast depolarization. Muon site populations shift above 325K.
AI.conclusion: Mn3Sn exhibits a highly dynamic and continuously evolving magnetic landscape where distinct magnetic orders (IT-AFM, IC helical, and FM-like components) coexist and transform with temperature. The proposed spin-glass state is refuted in favor of coexisting FM contributions and slowly fluctuating local moments, highlighting the intrinsic complexity of this AFM Weyl semimetal.

title: Bulk-Boundary Correspondence in Semi-Infinite Chains from Sublattice Zeros
summary: We provide an alternative derivation of the bulk-boundary correspondence for semi-infinite chains. To describe edge states, we analytically continue the usual Bloch Hamiltonian to complex wave vectors $k$. To start, we note that the zeros of a Bloch wavefunction are related to edge states, at least in systems with nearest-neighbour hoppings. We show that an analytically continued Bloch Hamiltonian with chiral symmetry has exceptional points, where two different states coalesce. These special points are related to the adiabatic protection of edge states. We derive a winding number that counts the number of topological edge states protected by chiral symmetry.

AI.tldr: The paper offers an alternative derivation of the bulk-boundary correspondence for semi-infinite chains by analytically continuing the Bloch Hamiltonian to complex wave vectors. It shows that edge states are related to zeros of Bloch wavefunctions and that analytically continued Bloch Hamiltonians with chiral symmetry exhibit exceptional points where states coalesce. These exceptional points underpin the adiabatic protection of edge states, leading to a winding number that counts chiral-symmetry-protected topological edge states.
AI.motivation: To provide a new, more direct derivation of the bulk-boundary correspondence—the relationship between bulk topological invariants and the existence of protected edge states—without relying on conventional approaches that may obscure the physical mechanisms underlying edge-state protection.
AI.method: The authors analytically continue the Bloch Hamiltonian to complex wave vectors k in semi-infinite chains. They establish a connection between zeros of Bloch wavefunctions and edge states for nearest-neighbour hopping systems. They then analyze the analytically continued Hamiltonian under chiral symmetry, identifying exceptional points where two distinct states coalesce, and use these to construct a winding number counting topological edge states.
AI.result: The analytical continuation approach reveals that exceptional points of the complex-momentum Bloch Hamiltonian correspond to the adiabatic protection of edge states in chiral-symmetric systems, and a winding number can be defined that counts the number of topologically protected edge states.
AI.conclusion: The bulk-boundary correspondence can be derived through analytic continuation of the Bloch Hamiltonian to complex wave vectors, with exceptional points and Bloch-wavefunction zeros providing a direct and physically transparent route to counting chiral-symmetry-protected edge states.

title: Cryogenic focused-ion-beam microstructuring enabling quantitative $c$-axis transport measurements in Tl$_2$Ba$_2$CuO$_{6+δ}$
summary: Absolute transport measurements in correlated quantum materials are often limited by disorder, inhomogeneity, geometric uncertainty, and small crystal size. Focused ion beam (FIB) technology offers a route to overcome many of these limitations by enabling transport devices with precisely defined geometry to be fabricated from lamellae extracted from carefully selected regions of a crystal, but its application to cuprate superconductors has been hindered by ion-beam-induced damage. Here we study the clean overdoped cuprate Tl2201 and show that conventional FIB processing causes thermally driven oxygen loss, while cryogenic FIB microstructuring largely suppresses this degradation and preserves the crystal structure from the bulk to the atomic scale. Microstructured devices quantitatively reproduce established in-plane resistivity and Hall carrier density measurements without rescaling. Applying this approach to $c$-axis transport, we obtain absolute $ρ_c(T)$ values approximately three times larger than previously reported, bringing the transport anisotropy into quantitative agreement with the known Fermi surface geometry within an isotropic relaxation-time approximation. These results resolve a long-standing discrepancy between transport and quantum oscillation measurements in overdoped Tl2201 and establish cryogenic FIB microstructuring as a route to reliable quantitative transport measurements in quantum materials where disorder, inhomogeneity, geometry, or small crystal size have previously limited experimental accuracy.

AI.tldr: Cryogenic focused ion beam (FIB) microstructuring preserves oxygen stoichiometry in the overdoped cuprate Tl2201, unlike conventional FIB which causes thermally driven oxygen loss. This enables quantitative c-axis transport measurements revealing resistivity values ~3x larger than previously reported, resolving a long-standing discrepancy between transport and quantum oscillation measurements and establishing cryo-FIB as a reliable route for quantitative transport in correlated quantum materials.
AI.motivation: Absolute transport measurements in correlated quantum materials are often limited by disorder, inhomogeneity, geometric uncertainty, and small crystal size. While FIB enables precisely defined transport devices from selected crystal regions, its application to cuprate superconductors has been hindered by ion-beam-induced damage.
AI.method: The authors compare conventional FIB processing with cryogenic FIB microstructuring on clean overdoped Tl2201. Cryo-FIB suppresses thermally driven oxygen loss and preserves crystal structure from bulk to atomic scale. They then fabricate microstructured devices for c-axis transport measurements and compare results with established in-plane resistivity and Hall carrier density data, as well as Fermi surface geometry within an isotropic relaxation-time approximation.
AI.result: Cryo-FIB microstructured devices quantitatively reproduce established in-plane resistivity and Hall carrier density without rescaling. For c-axis transport, absolute ρ_c(T) values are approximately three times larger than previously reported, bringing transport anisotropy into quantitative agreement with known Fermi surface geometry within an isotropic relaxation-time approximation.
AI.conclusion: The results resolve a long-standing discrepancy between transport and quantum oscillation measurements in overdoped Tl2201, and establish cryogenic FIB microstructuring as a viable route to reliable quantitative transport measurements in quantum materials where disorder, inhomogeneity, geometry, or small crystal size have previously limited experimental accuracy.

title: Quantum resetting with memory
summary: We introduce a quantum stochastic resetting protocol with uniform memory, in which each resetting event returns the system to a state visited at a time chosen uniformly from its entire history. The resulting dynamics is nonunitary, non-Markovian and a direct quantum generalization of the classical preferential relocation model. Working in the energy eigenbasis, we derive the exact evolution of every density-matrix element for an arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonian and show that the Hamiltonian enters the dynamics only through the corresponding Bohr frequencies. This leads to a natural distinction between two classes of quantum systems: gapped and gapless. In \emph{gapped systems} (systems with a discrete energy spectrum), while the diagonal elements remain unchanged, the off-diagonal elements of the density matrix in the energy eigenbasis decay algebraically with a continuously varying exponent and with an amplitude that oscillates periodically in $\log t$. The system therefore approaches a stationary state that is independent of the resetting rate and retains a strong memory of the initial state. In \emph{gapless systems} (systems with a continuous energy spectrum), arbitrarily small Bohr frequencies prevent stationarity. Instead, the position distribution spreads on the universal (ultra-slow) scale $\log(rt)/r$, independently of the initial state and of the details of the Hamiltonian. We illustrate these results with a two-level system, a harmonic oscillator, and a free quantum particle, and contrast them with their classical counterparts.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a quantum stochastic resetting protocol with uniform memory, where each reset returns the system to a state uniformly sampled from its entire history. For arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonians, exact evolution of density-matrix elements is derived, revealing two distinct classes: gapped systems exhibit algebraic decay of off-diagonal coherence with stationary states retaining initial-state memory, while gapless systems show ultra-slow universal spreading on the scale log(rt)/r without reaching stationarity.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to generalize the classical preferential relocation model to the quantum domain by introducing a resetting protocol with uniform memory, and to understand how the non-Markovian, nonunitary nature of this protocol affects quantum dynamics across different spectral classes of systems.
AI.method: The authors work in the energy eigenbasis and derive exact evolution equations for every density-matrix element under a uniform-memory quantum stochastic resetting protocol. They show the Hamiltonian enters only through Bohr frequencies, enabling a classification into gapped (discrete spectrum) and gapless (continuous spectrum) systems. They illustrate the framework with a two-level system, a harmonic oscillator, and a free quantum particle.
AI.result: In gapped systems, diagonal density-matrix elements remain unchanged while off-diagonal elements decay algebraically with a continuously varying exponent and an amplitude oscillating periodically in log t, approaching a resetting-rate-independent stationary state retaining initial-state memory. In gapless systems, arbitrarily small Bohr frequencies prevent stationarity, and the position distribution spreads on a universal ultra-slow scale log(rt)/r independent of initial state and Hamiltonian details.
AI.conclusion: The quantum uniform-memory resetting protocol reveals a sharp dichotomy between gapped and gapless quantum systems: gapped systems reach memory-retaining stationary states via algebraic decoherence, whereas gapless systems never equilibrate and instead exhibit ultra-slow universal spreading. These behaviors differ fundamentally from their classical counterparts.

title: Transient Liquid Phase Bonding of NiTi Using Cu- and Nb-base Interlayers
summary: Transient liquid phase (TLP) bonding was examined as an approach for joining NiTi to achieve a high joint efficiency while minimizing chemical variance within the joint region. Two bonding interlayer chemistries (Cu-base and Nb-base) were identified by screening thermodynamic criteria for TLP in ternary alloys using the CALPHAD method. These two systems were then experimentally evaluated with respect to their impact on solidification kinetics, microstructure in the joint region, and performance during quasistatic and cyclic tensile loading. For both interlayer chemistries, the composition profile and microstructure in the joint region confirmed an isothermal solidification mechanism. In addition, the joints were found to be fully dense and contain at most 1.2% intermetallic phases. Tensile testing showed excellent load transfer across the joints with approximately 4% recoverable strain and martensite onset stresses reaching 94% and 89% of the unbonded, annealed NiTi values for Cu-base and Nb-base interlayers, respectively. Lastly, a stable superelastic response was observed under cyclic loading for both bond chemistries, with spatial variation in the strain evolution linked to enhanced stiffness and hardness in the joint region arising from the substitutional Cu and Nb solutes, as confirmed via nanoindentation. This study demonstrates that TLP bonding of NiTi can produce high-strength and nearly intermetallic-free joints without sacrificing functional performance, such as the superelastic response.

AI.tldr: This study demonstrates that transient liquid phase (TLP) bonding can join NiTi shape memory alloys using Cu-base and Nb-base interlayer chemistries selected via CALPHAD thermodynamic screening. The resulting joints are nearly intermetallic-free (≤1.2%), fully dense, achieve ~4% recoverable strain, and maintain martensite onset stresses at 89–94% of unbonded NiTi, with stable superelastic cyclic response.
AI.motivation: To develop a joining approach for NiTi that achieves high joint efficiency while minimizing chemical variation and intermetallic formation in the joint region, thereby preserving the alloy's functional properties such as superelasticity.
AI.method: Two interlayer chemistries (Cu-base and Nb-base) were screened using CALPHAD thermodynamic criteria for TLP in ternary alloys, then experimentally evaluated for solidification kinetics, joint microstructure, and mechanical performance under quasistatic and cyclic tensile loading, with nanoindentation used to assess local mechanical property variations.
AI.result: Both interlayer systems confirmed isothermal solidification with fully dense joints containing at most 1.2% intermetallic phases. Tensile testing showed ~4% recoverable strain, martensite onset stresses reaching 94% (Cu-base) and 89% (Nb-base) of unbonded NiTi values, and stable superelastic response under cyclic loading with strain evolution linked to enhanced stiffness/hardness from substitutional solutes.
AI.conclusion: TLP bonding can produce high-strength, nearly intermetallic-free NiTi joints without sacrificing functional performance, including stable superelastic response, offering a viable joining solution for NiTi components.

title: Pressure-Driven Evolution of Electronic and Magnetic Correlations in Bilayer Nickelate La3Ni2O7
summary: The recent discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in pressurized bilayer La3Ni2O7 has sparked intense research interest, yet the microscopic mechanism governing its pressure-dependent superconducting transition temperature (Tc) remains elusive. In this work, we investigate the electronic and magnetic correlations of La3Ni2O7 under high pressure using a combination of density-functional theory (DFT), constrained random phase approximation (cRPA), and dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). We find that while hydrostatic pressure enhances the interlayer hopping and the bare superexchange energy scale (4t2/U), it simultaneously drives the system toward a more itinerant regime by reducing the relative correlation strength (U/W). Crucially, our results reveal a distinct orbital-selective evolution: the Ni dx2-y2 states become increasingly itinerant, whereas the Ni dz2 orbitals retain a more localized character. This pressure-induced itinerancy significantly enhances the hybridization between the two, leading to a dramatic amplification of the Kondo-like screening of the local dz2 moments by the itinerant dx2-y2 electrons. Consequently, the effective magnetic exchange coupling (Jeff), which serves as the pairing glue, is suppressed in the high-pressure regime. Our findings suggest that the monotonic decrease of Tc at high pressures is driven by the dominance of Kondo screening over superexchange interactions, providing a coherent microscopic explanation for the dome-shaped superconducting phase diagram in La3Ni2O7.

AI.tldr: Using DFT+cRPA+DMFT, the authors show that pressure in La3Ni2O7 enhances interlayer hopping and itinerancy (especially of Ni dx2-y2 states), which amplifies Kondo-like screening of local dz2 moments. This suppresses the effective magnetic exchange coupling (Jeff) and explains the dome-shaped Tc versus pressure phase diagram.
AI.motivation: The microscopic mechanism behind the pressure-dependent superconducting transition temperature in pressurized bilayer La3Ni2O7 remains unclear; understanding why Tc decreases at high pressures is needed.
AI.method: First-principles electronic structure calculations combining density-functional theory (DFT), constrained random phase approximation (cRPA), and dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) under hydrostatic pressure.
AI.result: Pressure increases interlayer hopping and bare superexchange (4t2/U) but reduces U/W toward a more itinerant regime. Orbital-selective evolution occurs: Ni dx2-y2 states become itinerant while dz2 orbitals remain localized. This enhances hybridization and Kondo-like screening of dz2 moments, suppressing the effective magnetic exchange coupling Jeff in the high-pressure regime.
AI.conclusion: The monotonic decrease of Tc at high pressures is driven by the dominance of Kondo screening over superexchange interactions, providing a coherent microscopic explanation for the dome-shaped superconducting phase diagram in La3Ni2O7.

title: Layer-Hybridized Wigner Crystals in MoSe2/WS2 Moiré Superlattice
summary: Transition metal dichalcogenide moiré heterobilayers with type-II band alignment provide a versatile platform for layer-polarized generalized Wigner crystals, in which strong Coulomb interactions drive charge ordering at fractional lattice fillings. With a finite interlayer band offset, an out-of-plane electric field can tune layer-resolved moiré bands through resonance and enable controllable interlayer hybridization. Although hybridized Mott insulators have been previously demonstrated, whether fractional charge-ordered states can survive such hybridization remains elusive. Here we drive an H-stacked MoSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayer through a type-I-to-type-II band-alignment transition and realize layer-hybridized Mott insulator and generalized Wigner crystals. For fillings below one electron per moiré cell, tunneling delocalizes electrons and modifies Wigner crystallization. However, above one electron per cell, Coulomb repulsion overcomes tunneling and favors layer-separated occupation, stabilizing stronger charge-ordered states. These results establish electrically tunable hybridized moiré heterobilayers as a powerful platform for engineering correlated charge order and exploring fractional Chern phases and emergent magnetism.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that in H-stacked MoSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayers, an out-of-plane electric field can drive a type-I-to-type-II band-alignment transition, realizing layer-hybridized Mott insulators and generalized Wigner crystals. Below one electron per moiré cell, interlayer tunneling delocalizes electrons and weakens Wigner crystallization, while above one electron per cell, Coulomb repulsion dominates tunneling, favoring layer-separated occupation and stabilizing stronger charge-ordered states.
AI.motivation: To determine whether fractional charge-ordered states (generalized Wigner crystals) can survive interlayer hybridization in transition metal dichalcogenide moiré heterobilayers, since hybridized Mott insulators have been demonstrated but the fate of fractional charge-ordered states under controllable interlayer hybridization remained elusive.
AI.method: The authors use an H-stacked MoSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayer with type-II band alignment and apply an out-of-plane electric field to tune the layer-resolved moiré bands through resonance, driving the system through a type-I-to-type-II band-alignment transition and inducing controllable interlayer hybridization.
AI.result: They realize layer-hybridized Mott insulators and generalized Wigner crystals. For fillings below one electron per moiré cell, tunneling delocalizes electrons and modifies Wigner crystallization. Above one electron per cell, Coulomb repulsion overcomes tunneling and favors layer-separated occupation, stabilizing stronger charge-ordered states.
AI.conclusion: Electrically tunable hybridized moiré heterobilayers constitute a powerful platform for engineering correlated charge order, with potential for exploring fractional Chern phases and emergent magnetism.

title: Superconducting ternary compounds Li-X-B (X=Mo, W) within the mild pressure range: First-principles predictions
summary: Among the superconducting hydrides under high pressure, a number of studies concentrate on the ternary compounds to explore unique superconductors, which are capable of reducing the stable pressure and maintain superconductivity. In this work, to verify our proposed strategy of ternary composition lines (TCLs) to explore ternary compounds, we combined the first-principles calculations and crystal structure predictions to study the ternary compounds Li-X-B (X=Mo, W) under high pressure. After calculations along five and four TCLs in Li-W-B and Li-Mo-B, respectively, five Li-W-B compounds and four Li-Mo-B compounds were predicted. The compositions of LiWB4, Li4MoB2 and LiMo2B2 could be thermodynamically stable under high pressure, and Li2WB6 is around 0.02 eV/atom above the convex hull at 0 GPa, which has potential for synthesizing. Both of the predicted Li2WB6 P6/mmm and Li2WB4 R-3m are superconducting and their Tc are around 11 K, which are similar to the Tc of WB2 P6/mmm around 100 GPa. An anomalous increase of Tc was found in Li4MoB2 C2/m upon compression. We carried out full ternary search (FTS) to evaluate the validity of the TCLs strategy in Li-W-B system at 0 GPa. Our results are helpful for understanding the phase diagram of Li-X-B (X=Mo, W) under high pressure and the introducing of Li atoms provide candidate structures to reduce the measured stable pressure from ~100 GPa in WB2 P6/mmm to 0 GPa. Meanwhile, we preliminary validate the strategy of TCLs in structure predictions and we expect to improve this strategy in the future, shedding light on the studies of ternary compounds.

AI.tldr: This paper uses first-principles calculations and crystal structure predictions to investigate ternary Li-X-B (X=Mo, W) compounds under high pressure, validating a proposed "ternary composition lines" (TCLs) strategy. Nine new compounds are predicted, several thermodynamically stable under pressure, with Li2WB6 and Li2WB4 showing superconductivity around 11 K. Introducing Li atoms reduces the stable pressure from ~100 GPa in WB2 to 0 GPa.
AI.motivation: To explore ternary superconducting hydride-type compounds that can reduce the stable pressure required for superconductivity, and to validate a proposed TCLs strategy for efficiently searching ternary compound space.
AI.method: Combined first-principles calculations with crystal structure predictions, searching along five TCLs in Li-W-B and four TCLs in Li-Mo-B systems. Full ternary search (FTS) was performed to validate the TCLs strategy in Li-W-B at 0 GPa.
AI.result: Five Li-W-B and four Li-Mo-B compounds were predicted. LiWB4, Li4MoB2, and LiMo2B2 are thermodynamically stable under high pressure; Li2WB6 is ~0.02 eV/atom above the convex hull at 0 GPa with synthesis potential. Li2WB6 (P6/mmm) and Li2WB4 (R-3m) are superconducting with Tc ~11 K, comparable to WB2 at ~100 GPa. An anomalous Tc increase was found in Li4MoB2 (C2/m) under compression.
AI.conclusion: The TCLs strategy is preliminarily validated as an efficient approach for predicting ternary compounds. Introducing Li atoms into WB2-type structures reduces the stable pressure from ~100 GPa to 0 GPa, and the results provide insight into the high-pressure phase diagrams of Li-X-B (X=Mo, W) systems.

title: An essay on $d_0$ in neutron-based strain measurement techniques: equilibrium-based methods for non-destructive $d_0$ estimation
summary: Determination of the stress-free reference lattice spacing, $d_0$, is a central and often underestimated difficulty in diffraction-based strain measurement. Although commonly treated as a material constant, $d_0$ often varies with position and measurement direction as a result of composition, phase, texture and residual stress at the sub-bulk scale. While direct measurement of $d_0$ from coupons is usually preferable, this is sometimes impractical or even impossible. This paper reviews the $d_0$ problem in general and develops a hierarchy of non-destructive alternatives based on mechanical equilibrium. This ranges from established techniques based on force-balance, to the application of boundary conditions and finally an approach based on point-wise equilibrium within a sample, implemented through eigenstrain analysis. In all cases, examples are provided in the form of real samples including an additively manufactured Inconel cube, ancient Roman bronze medical probes and an ancient bronze dagger of purported Persian origin. These latter examples demonstrate that equilibrium can provide a practical physical constraint for estimating $d_0$ when destructive reference measurements are entirely inappropriate.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the challenges of determining the stress-free reference lattice spacing (d0) in diffraction-based strain measurement and develops a hierarchy of non-destructive alternatives based on mechanical equilibrium—ranging from force-balance techniques to boundary condition applications and point-wise equilibrium via eigenstrain analysis—demonstrated on additively manufactured Inconel, ancient Roman bronze, and an ancient Persian dagger.
AI.motivation: The d0 problem is a central but often underestimated difficulty in diffraction-based strain measurement. Although commonly treated as a material constant, d0 varies with position and direction due to composition, phase, texture, and residual stress. Direct measurement from coupons is sometimes impractical or impossible, especially for precious or irreplaceable samples, necessitating non-destructive alternatives.
AI.method: The paper develops a hierarchy of non-destructive methods for estimating d0 based on mechanical equilibrium principles: (1) established force-balance techniques, (2) application of boundary conditions, and (3) point-wise equilibrium within a sample implemented through eigenstrain analysis. Each approach is demonstrated on real samples.
AI.result: The techniques were successfully applied to an additively manufactured Inconel cube, ancient Roman bronze medical probes, and an ancient bronze dagger of purported Persian origin, demonstrating that mechanical equilibrium provides a practical physical constraint for estimating d0 when destructive reference measurements are entirely inappropriate.
AI.conclusion: Equilibrium-based approaches provide a viable, non-destructive hierarchy of methods for determining d0 in diffraction-based strain measurements, particularly valuable for irreplaceable cultural heritage objects where destructive reference measurement is unacceptable.

title: Long and short time linear response of metals: a geometric approach
summary: The time-dependent quantum geometric tensor, which captures dipole fluctuations of bound electrons, is essential for understanding the electronic properties of insulators, superconductors, and flat bands. It is often considered subleading for low-energy descriptions of metals that are dominated by intra-band processes. Here, we revisit this perspective and highlight scenarios where the quantum geometry of the wavefunctions close to the Fermi surface plays a significant role. We compute the time-dependent quantum geometric tensor for metals, explain its divergence, and contrast it against singular geometric tensors of Dirac and Weyl semi-metals. We identify the ratio of Drude to total spectral weight, $D/\mathcal{S}_1$, as a lattice-scale probe of bound versus itinerant charge, and quantify it in the kagome metal, where the two van Hove fillings respond differently despite identical Fermi surfaces.

AI.tldr: The paper revisits the role of quantum geometry in metals, showing that the time-dependent quantum geometric tensor—typically considered subleading for metallic descriptions—plays a significant role near the Fermi surface. The authors compute this tensor for metals, explain its divergence, contrast it with singular geometric tensors of Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and introduce D/S₁ (ratio of Drude to total spectral weight) as a lattice-scale probe of bound versus itinerant charge, demonstrated in kagome metals where different van Hove fillings respond differently despite identical Fermi surfaces.
AI.motivation: Quantum geometric tensors are usually ignored in metallic systems because intra-band processes dominate low-energy descriptions. The authors challenge this view by identifying scenarios where quantum geometry near the Fermi surface is significant, and propose a new experimental probe to distinguish bound from itinerant charge.
AI.method: The authors compute the time-dependent quantum geometric tensor for metallic systems, analyze its divergence behavior, and compare it against the singular geometric tensors found in Dirac and Weyl semimetals. They define the ratio D/S₁ (Drude weight to total spectral weight) as a lattice-scale probe and quantify it in kagome metals at different van Hove fillings.
AI.result: The time-dependent quantum geometric tensor in metals diverges and shows behavior distinct from Dirac/Weyl semimetals. The D/S₁ ratio serves as a robust lattice-scale probe of bound versus itinerant charge, and in the kagome metal, the two van Hove fillings exhibit different responses despite having identical Fermi surfaces, revealing the subtle role of quantum geometry.
AI.conclusion: Quantum geometry near the Fermi surface is not always subleading in metals. The D/S₁ ratio provides a new diagnostic tool for characterizing electronic correlations at the lattice scale, with kagome metals offering a clear platform to observe these geometric effects.

title: Non-linear spin current in the surface states of topological insulators
summary: Spin Hall effect is one of the primary sources of pure spin current in spintronic devices, observed in spin-orbit coupled materials. In this work, we investigate linear and non-linear pure spin currents in the hexagonally warped surface states of topological insulators like $\rm Bi_2Te_3$, using the formalism of conserved spin transport. The hexagonal warping effect enables the application of this formalism by providing a well-defined Berry curvature without breaking the time-reversal symmetry. The absence of in-plane spin currents in the linear response motivates the extension of the formalism to the non-linear regime, by combining the perturbation of Bloch states with the Boltzmann transport equation. The second-order response exhibits both intrinsic and extrinsic in-plane spin currents induced by the spin-weighted Berry curvature, Berry connection polarizability (BCP) dipole and Berry curvature dipole (BCD) respectively. The band anisotropy due to the $C_{3v}$ symmetry of the material ($\rm Bi_2Te_3$) propagates through the spin textures and the band geometric quantities, resulting in the selection of certain components of the spin conductivity tensors.

AI.tldr: This work investigates linear and nonlinear pure spin currents in the hexagonally warped surface states of topological insulators (e.g., Bi2Te3) using conserved spin transport formalism. The hexagonal warping provides a well-defined Berry curvature without breaking time-reversal symmetry. While linear response yields no in-plane spin currents, the second-order response produces intrinsic and extrinsic in-plane spin currents via spin-weighted Berry curvature, BCP dipole, and BCD effects, with C3v symmetry dictating which spin conductivity tensor components are selected.
AI.motivation: Spin Hall effect is a key source of pure spin currents in spintronic devices obtained in spin-orbit coupled materials, yet the hexagonal warping of topological insulator surface states presents a unique venue where linear in-plane spin currents vanish, necessitating an extension to the nonlinear regime to generate such currents.
AI.method: Conserved spin transport formalism combined with hexagonal warping-induced Berry curvature in topological insulator surface states. The approach extends from the perturbation of Bloch states to the Boltzmann transport equation to treat second-order responses.
AI.result: Second-order response yields both intrinsic (spin-weighted Berry curvature) and extrinsic (BCP dipole and BCD) in-plane spin currents. C3v symmetry leads to selection of specific components of the spin conductivity tensors through band anisotropy propagation into spin textures and geometric quantities.
AI.conclusion: The hexagonal warping enables a well-defined Berry curvature for conserved spin transport studies, and the nonlinear regime unlocks in-plane spin currents absent at linear order, with symmetry selection rules determining the allowed conductivity tensor components in Bi2Te3.

title: Emergence of Double-Dome Superconductivity in the Pressurized Dirac Semimetal BaMg2Bi2
summary: Dirac semimetal BaMg2Bi2 is reported to be a unique topological material that manifests surface superconductivity that coexistswith bulk band topology at ambient pressure. Here, we present a comprehensive investigation of high-pressure superconductingproperties in BaMg2Bi2 single crystal. Significantly, a pressure-driven double-dome superconducting behavior was revealed, withthe superconducting transition temperature Tc approaching the maximum values of 6.67 K at 4.5 GPa and 7.22 K at 10.4 GPafor the first and second superconducting domes, respectively. The combination of high-pressure X-ray diffraction, Hall resistivitymeasurements, and theoretical calculations demonstrates that, the first superconducting regime is closely related to the pressure-modulated Lifshitz transition, whereas the second superconducting phase emerges concurrently with a structural transition fromthe ambient-pressure P3m1 phase to a high-pressure Pnma phase.

AI.tldr: High-pressure studies on BaMg2Bi2 single crystals reveal a double-dome superconducting behavior with Tc maxima of 6.67 K at 4.5 GPa and 7.22 K at 10.4 GPa, driven respectively by a Lifshitz transition and a structural transition from P3m1 to Pnma phases.
AI.motivation: To comprehensively investigate high-pressure superconducting properties in the Dirac semimetal BaMg2Bi2, a topological material with surface superconductivity coexisting with bulk band topology at ambient pressure, in order to understand the pressure-driven evolution of its superconductivity.
AI.method: High-pressure superconducting property measurements on BaMg2Bi2 single crystals, combined with high-pressure X-ray diffraction, Hall resistivity measurements, and theoretical calculations.
AI.result: A pressure-driven double-dome superconducting behavior was discovered: Tc peaks at 6.67 K at 4.5 GPa (first dome) and 7.22 K at 10.4 GPa (second dome). The first superconducting regime correlates with a pressure-modulated Lifshitz transition, while the second superconducting phase coincides with a structural transition from the ambient P3m1 phase to a high-pressure Pnma phase.
AI.conclusion: The double-dome superconductivity in BaMg2Bi2 arises from two distinct mechanisms: the first dome is linked to electronic band structure changes via a Lifshitz transition, while the second dome is associated with a structural phase transition, revealing interplay between topology, structure, and superconductivity under pressure.

title: The AFLOW Library of Crystallographic Prototypes: Part 5
summary: The AFLOW library of crystallographic prototypes has been updated to incorporate an additional 344 entries, which now reaches 2,127 prototypes. ICSD and CCDC numbers have been added to the website alongside improvements to the user interface. New tutorials covering the basics of crystallography in the context of materials science have also been added. Lastly, we covered the current known applications of AFLOW prototype labels and materials data across research software.

AI.tldr: The AFLOW library of crystallographic prototypes has been expanded to 2,127 entries with 344 new additions, improved user interface with ICSD and CCDC number links, new crystallography tutorials, and a review of applications of AFLOW prototype labels across research software.
AI.motivation: To update and expand the AFLOW crystallographic prototype library to better serve the materials science community by adding more prototype entries, improving accessibility, and documenting the library's usage across research software.
AI.method: Incorporated 344 additional crystallographic prototype entries into the AFLOW library, added ICSD and CCDC database numbers to the website, improved the user interface, created crystallography tutorials for materials science context, and surveyed the applications of AFLOW prototype labels in research software.
AI.result: The AFLOW library now contains 2,127 prototypes total. The website includes database cross-references (ICSD/CCDC numbers), enhanced UI, educational tutorials, and a comprehensive overview of how AFLOW prototype labels are used in research software.
AI.conclusion: The AFLOW prototype library continues to grow as a comprehensive resource for crystallographic prototypes, with improved usability, educational content, and documented interoperability with other research software.

title: Optimized Tensor-Network Renormalization for Quantum Dynamics: Resolving the Spectral Function of $\mathrm{K_2Co(SeO_3)_2}$
summary: Tensor-network methods have opened a powerful route for the study of dynamical spectral functions in two-dimensional quantum systems. However, existing approaches within the framework of infinite projected entangled-pair states construct the required renormalization tensors solely from the ground-state environment and can suffer from severe numerical instability. We identify the origin of this instability and introduce an excitation-tailored corner-transfer-matrix renormalization-group (ET-CTMRG) method to resolve it. By incorporating excitation tensors into the renormalization procedure, the method constructs a substantially more accurate effective Hamiltonian matrix and thereby yields reliable and well-converged excitation spectra. For Heisenberg antiferromagnets, it reduces truncation errors by orders of magnitude and for the particularly complex case of the supersolid phase in the triangular-lattice XXZ magnet $\mathrm{K_2Co(SeO_3)_2}$, it achieves excellent quantitative agreement with inelastic neutron-scattering measurements. ET-CTMRG therefore provides a robust framework for investigating the dynamical properties of strongly correlated quantum systems.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an excitation-tailored corner-transfer-matrix renormalization-group (ET-CTMRG) method that incorporates excitation tensors into the renormalization procedure for infinite projected entangled-pair states, resolving numerical instabilities in existing approaches and yielding well-converged dynamical spectral functions for two-dimensional quantum systems.
AI.motivation: Existing tensor-network approaches for computing dynamical spectral functions in 2D quantum systems construct renormalization tensors solely from the ground-state environment, which can suffer from severe numerical instability when computing excitations.
AI.method: The method, ET-CTMRG, incorporates excitation tensors directly into the corner-transfer-matrix renormalization-group procedure, thereby constructing a substantially more accurate effective Hamiltonian matrix for computing excitation spectra within the infinite projected entangled-pair state framework.
AI.result: For Heisenberg antiferromagnets, ET-CTMRG reduces truncation errors by orders of magnitude. For the supersolid phase in the triangular-lattice XXZ magnet K2Co(SeO3)2, it achieves excellent quantitative agreement with inelastic neutron-scattering measurements.
AI.conclusion: ET-CTMRG provides a robust and accurate framework for investigating dynamical properties of strongly correlated quantum systems, overcoming the numerical instabilities of prior tensor-network approaches.

title: Wannier-Stark localization, confinement and edge states
comment: Accepted for publication in Am. J. Phys
summary: The boundary between a system's bulk and the vacuum can be modeled by a potential which confines the electrons to the bulk. Here we present the example of the Wannier-Stark linear potential, generated by an electric field along one axis of a two-dimensional lattice. Along that axis, the potential generates electronic states which are localized around each lattice site, with eigenenergies which form the Wannier-Stark ladder. In the transverse direction, the states are governed by a tight binding model with free Bloch states. In the ground state, filling these states under the Pauli principle generates an insulating bulk and an edge which can be metallic in the transverse direction. This paper explains the concepts of localization, localization length, filling and confinement. The paper also acquaints the readers with the use of Bessel functions in the solution of a simple physical model. These topics can be easily included in courses on solid state physics, and only require prior knowledge of quantum mechanics.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the Wannier-Stark linear potential as a pedagogical model for electron confinement at a system's boundary. An electric field along one axis of a 2D lattice produces localized electronic states (Wannier-Stark ladder) along that axis, while the transverse direction supports free Bloch states. Filling these states under the Pauli principle yields an insulating bulk with a potentially metallic edge. The paper introduces students to localization, localization length, filling, and confinement, and demonstrates the use of Bessel functions in solving a simple physical model.
AI.motivation: To provide a simple, pedagogically accessible physical model that illustrates the boundary between a system's bulk and vacuum, demonstrating concepts of confinement, localization, and metallic edge states that can be easily incorporated into solid state physics courses.
AI.method: The paper uses the Wannier-Stark linear potential—created by an electric field along one axis of a two-dimensional lattice—to model electron confinement. Along the field axis, eigenstates localize around lattice sites forming a Wannier-Stark ladder; in the transverse direction, states follow a tight-binding model with free Bloch states. The ground state filling under the Pauli exclusion principle is analyzed to derive the bulk insulating and potentially metallic edge behavior.
AI.result: The model yields an insulating bulk and an edge that can be metallic in the transverse direction when the Wannier-Stark ladder states are filled according to the Pauli principle. The solution naturally involves Bessel functions, providing a concrete application of these special functions in a physics context.
AI.conclusion: The paper offers a clear, self-contained pedagogical framework for teaching concepts of localization, localization length, filling, and confinement in solid state physics. It requires only prior knowledge of quantum mechanics and can be readily incorporated into existing course curricula.

title: Screening phonon-mediated superconductors from static orbital Hamiltonians
summary: The first-principles search for superconductors is severely limited by the high cost of electron-phonon coupling (EPC) calculations. Here we develop a low-cost, physically transparent framework that identifies strong-EPC materials directly from static orbital-based Hamiltonians without explicit phonon perturbation calculations. Verification using density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) for representative superconductors shows that the framework captures semi-quantitatively the EPC scale at substantially lower computational cost. Applied to more than 36,000 compounds in the MattKeyBond database, it identifies 34 dynamically stable superconducting candidates with calculated $T_c > 10$ K after DFPT verification. These candidates reveal two distinct routes to relatively high-$T_c$ superconductivity: a metallized covalent $σ$-bond route that is more favorable for achieving high-$T_c$ superconductors, and a Fermi-level density-of-states accumulation route that can enhance $T_c$ but usually to a more limited extent.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a low-cost, physically transparent framework that identifies strong electron-phonon coupling (EPC) superconductors directly from static orbital-based Hamiltonians, bypassing expensive phonon perturbation calculations. Applied to 36,000+ compounds, it finds 34 dynamically stable superconducting candidates with Tc > 10 K after DFPT verification. Two routes to high-Tc superconductivity are revealed: metallized covalent σ-bond route (more favorable for high Tc) and Fermi-level density-of-states accumulation route (more limited enhancement).
AI.motivation: First-principles searches for superconductors are severely bottlenecked by the high computational cost of electron-phonon coupling (EPC) calculations, limiting the scope of materials screening.
AI.method: The framework predicts strong-EPC materials directly from static orbital-based Hamiltonians without explicit phonon perturbation calculations. Verification uses density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) for representative superconductors, and large-scale screening is applied to over 36,000 compounds in the MattKeyBond database.
AI.result: The framework captures semi-quantitatively the EPC scale at substantially lower computational cost compared to DFPT. Screening identifies 34 dynamically stable superconducting candidates with calculated Tc > 10 K after DFPT verification, revealing two distinct physical routes to relatively high-Tc superconductivity (metallized covalent σ-bond route and Fermi-level density-of-states accumulation route).
AI.conclusion: The metallized covalent σ-bond route appears more favorable for achieving high-Tc superconductors, while the Fermi-level density-of-states accumulation route enhances Tc to a more limited extent, providing physical insight for future superconductor discovery.

title: Machine Learning Compatible CALPHAD-type Optimization from Phase Equilibria by Auto-differentiation
summary: To accurately determine phase boundaries and phase transitions, thermodynamic models that describe free energies of phases often have to be optimized based on experimentally observed phase equilibria. While different approaches exist for thermodynamic optimizations, these approaches are often implemented in ways that are not compatible with machine learning workflows that requires differentiable calculation of loss function. In this work, we derive a phase equilibrium loss function based on thermodynamic potentials that can be efficiently evaluated and enable gradient based optimization by auto-differentiation in the PyTorch package. By minimizing this loss function, general thermodynamic model parameters can be optimized with respect to experimental phase equilibria data. Using thermodynamic models in the CALculation of PHAse Diagram (CALPHAD) framework, We illustrate successful and efficient optimization in different systems including ternary ones with more than 100 parameters. As the loss function is defined independently of the details of the thermodynamic models, it can be used to optimize machine learning thermodynamic models in general. In particular, we demonstrate a top-down optimization of atomistic potential from target phase equilibria.

AI.tldr: The paper derives a phase equilibrium loss function based on thermodynamic potentials that enables gradient-based optimization via auto-differentiation in PyTorch. This loss function allows general thermodynamic model parameters to be optimized against experimental phase equilibria data, demonstrated on CALPHAD models (including ternary systems with >100 parameters) and extending to top-down optimization of atomistic potentials from target phase equilibria.
AI.motivation: Thermodynamic models for determining phase boundaries often require optimization against experimental phase equilibria data, but existing optimization approaches are incompatible with machine learning workflows that need differentiable loss functions.
AI.method: The authors derive a phase equilibrium loss function from thermodynamic potentials that is efficiently evaluable and enables gradient-based optimization through auto-differentiation in PyTorch. The loss function is model-agnostic, defined independently of thermodynamic model details, making it applicable to both CALPHAD models and machine learning thermodynamic models.
AI.result: The approach successfully optimizes thermodynamic model parameters in systems including ternary ones with more than 100 parameters. It also demonstrates top-down optimization of atomistic potentials from target phase equilibria.
AI.conclusion: The proposed differentiable phase equilibrium loss function bridges thermodynamic optimization and machine learning workflows, enabling efficient parameter optimization across diverse thermodynamic models including both CALPHAD and atomistic potential frameworks.

title: Extracting higher-order nonlinearities in nanomechanical resonators using the backbone relation
summary: Nanomechanical resonators are a powerful platform for studying nonlinear dynamics with high sensitivity and precision. We explore the nonlinear response of a high-Q nanomechanical string resonator in and beyond the Duffing regime and introduce a robust framework for accurately extracting its conservative nonlinearities.
